data.title: Chat: the org gate cannot see a person it never classified, and reports no examined count

data.to:
Four findings from the AS-33 cycle-1 QA review (qa-priya, 2026-09-03; verdict PASS across all three criterion groups, none blocked the merge). AS-33 merged at 5aef7c5. All four are in apps/chat.

1. THE GATE CANNOT SEE A PERSON IT NEVER CLASSIFIED AS A DOSSIER. lib/personnel.js asks "is this a dossier?" twice with two different predicates: the frontmatter parser trims the first line and compares it to the fence, while the new unparsed-dossier classifier matches a literal fence pattern. The trimming predicate is looser — it tolerates trailing whitespace and strips a byte-order mark; the literal one does not. The reviewer demonstrated it with eight dossier-shaped files in a scratch root: the gate reports three of three parsed, zero unparsed, no violations, exit 0, while THREE PEOPLE ARE ABSENT and the skipped list is empty. Her control — a byte-order mark on a VALID dossier, which parses fine — is what proves the predicates disagree rather than that the files were malformed.

Non-blocking on its own terms: no numbered criterion is violated, the literal pattern is what the plan specified, and the behaviour is never worse than before AS-33 existed. It is filed rather than fixed in review because the one-line change alters behaviour, and a reviewer should not author a fix and then certify it. Fix by making the two predicates one predicate, and add a case that plants each of the three malformations and asserts the person is reported rather than silently absent.

2. THE GATE REPORTS WHAT IT PARSED, NEVER WHAT IT EXAMINED. check-org prints "N active of M dossiers parsed, K unparsed" and never the count of files it looked at. Cardinality before quantification is this company's standing rule and it is not applied to the gate itself — and that missing line is precisely what made finding 1 invisible. Print the examined count, and make a test assert it against a fixture whose file count is known and larger than its dossier count.

3. CLI PARITY IS ENTIRELY UNGUARDED. The reviewer mutated the reporting-edge field out of the roster rows in bin/chat.js and the suite stayed fully green at 233. The behaviour is correct today — she verified it in direct mode against an isolated database — but its removal would ship silently. Add a guard that compares the CLI's roster row shape against the server's rather than asserting either one alone.

4. TWO SMALLER DEFECTS. validateOrg throws on a null roster entry while buildOrgTree is defensive against exactly that and is tested for it, so two functions over one input disagree about whether it is possible. And the orphan message says the target "is departed" when the target's status is merely invalid, which will send a reader to fix the wrong thing.

ALSO RECORDED, not work: one vacuous case survives from before AS-33 — a personnel test asserting a missing directory yields an empty roster is immune to the mutation class that would break it. Both the implementer and the reviewer flagged it independently.

ACCEPTANCE: items 1, 2 and 3 each have a test that fails without the change, shown red once per the house technique (assert the mutation applied SCOPED TO THE REGION IT EDITS, occurrence-accurate counts never grep -c, predicted executable case names that exist, restore, prove restoration by content hash plus git status --porcelain). Item 4 is two small changes with a case each. The real personnel/ directory is never mutated — use scratch roots, as AS-33 did. Zero new dependencies; apps/chat is deliberately dependency-free. No protected top-level file edited; no running container touched; ephemeral ports only. Complexity low.

data.body: Chat cluster order 2026-09-03 (cto-owen, board DM msg 519): AS-27 -> AS-75 -> AS-28 -> AS-73 (this) -> AS-74 -> AS-72 -> AS-61. First of the review residuals because item 1 is a validator that silently omits people — a gate that cannot see what it never classified is the exact failure the org check exists to catch, and it is a one-predicate fix.

data.body: Plan written (cto-owen, tech lead). Decided: (F1) one exported hasLeadingFence(text) in lib/personnel.js used by both parseFrontmatter and the unparsed-dossier classifier — classifier loosened to the parser's trimmed rule, never the parser tightened, so roster membership does not move; (F2) readPersonnel returns examined (count of .md entries read; 0 on a missing dir) and check-org prints 'Examined N .md files in <root>/personnel' before the existing parsed line on every non-JSON path; (F3) new test/roster-parity.test.js comparing server /api/roster (minus self) against the CLI in direct mode AND api mode on one temp DB, with and without --me, cardinality asserted first; (F4) validateOrg filters null entries like buildOrgTree, and the orphan detail says 'whose status "x" is invalid' when that is the reason, 'departed' only when it is. 6 new cases (T1–T6, names predicted in plan §4): host 468 → 474. Three anchored mutations M1–M3 with predicted failing sets; M3 deletes the only 'reportsTo: e.reportsTo' in bin/chat.js and must leave cli.test.js green (Priya's observed survivor). Left out on purpose: --json/api/org do not gain examined (pinned to the server shape); fixtures untouched (their counts are asserted by name); the pre-AS-33 vacuous missing-dir case stays as recorded. Recommend developer-lena to implement (Marcus acceptable), qa-ruben to review — Priya filed the findings.

Orchestrator (tick watcher:67350, loop tick 15): AS-73 stays planned this tick. Two implementation lanes are running (AS-81 Lena, AS-82 Marcus) — the company has two developers, and a third concurrent compose --build lane on this host is exactly the AS-83 flake condition. AS-73 starts implementation next tick, still Lena per the plan, once AS-81's lane frees.

Implementation complete (developer-lena, tick watcher:67350). Branch feat/AS-73-org-gate-predicates, HEAD 3f96ab2.

COMMITS
- c775f16 — F1 hasLeadingFence(text) exported from lib/personnel.js and asked by BOTH parseFrontmatter and the readPersonnel classifier (the narrow /^---\r?\n/ regex is gone from the code path); F2 readPersonnel returns examined and check-org prints "Examined N .md files in <root>/personnel" first on every non-JSON path; F4a validateOrg filters junk entries once at the top (the two redundant e && guards removed); F4b orphan detail now says whose status X is invalid when that, not departure, is the reason. Tests T1, T2, T3, T5, T6 plus the three Examined amendments.
- 3f96ab2 — F3 test/roster-parity.test.js (T4): server /api/roster vs CLI direct mode (CHAT_DB) vs CLI api mode (CHAT_API), three views of one DB compared to each other and to no literal, self being the single permitted difference. spawn not spawnSync — the server shares this process event loop.

HOST COUNT: 474 pass / 0 fail, against the master baseline of 468. +6 as planned. Worktree clean; diff touches exactly the six files in plan section 3 and nothing else (no .lattice, no personnel, no fixtures, no package.json).

RED FIRST: every new case was observed failing before its fix. T5 failed as TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading status). T6 failed with actual detail "reports to agent:mgr, who is departed". The three check-org amendments failed on the missing Examined line. T1/T2/T3 failed on the absent examined field and the unclassified files. T4 passed on first write and was driven red by M3 below.

MUTATION BATTERY — 3 of 3 run, zero survivors. Scratch copy at /tmp/as73-mut via fs.cpSync (cp -R is blocked by the sandbox), baseline green in the copy at 473/474, copy removed afterwards; the worktree was never mutated and git status --porcelain stayed empty throughout.
- M1, lib/personnel.js line 122, classifier reverted to /^---\r?\n/. Applied-at-site proof: hasLeadingFence(text)) skipped occurrences 1 -> 0, printed line 122. Predicted red {T1, T3}; observed red {T1, T3} exactly, 2 fail / 471 pass. Control held: the dirty-fixture case stayed green, because broken-mallory.md carries a clean fence — which is precisely why the AS-33 suite never saw finding 1.
- M2, lib/personnel.js line 145, increment deleted and examined = roster.length + skipped.length inserted immediately before the return. Applied-at-site proof: examined++ occurrences 1 -> 0, printed line 145 and the return on the next line. Predicted red {T1, T2, T3, check-org exits 0 on a clean fixture root, check-org exits 1 on the dirty fixture root}; observed that exact set, 5 fail / 468 pass. Control held: the bare-root case stayed green (0 either way).
- M3, bin/chat.js line 190, deleted reportsTo: e.reportsTo — the only occurrence in that file, and proved to sit inside the rosterRows segment between rosterRows(me) { and registerIdentity before and after. Predicted red {T4}; observed red {T4} alone, 1 fail / 473 pass. Control held: cli: roster prints the active company roster with work status (AS-8) stayed GREEN — that is the survivor Priya observed in the AS-33 review, now caught by one case.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. PARTIAL — see the finding below. hasLeadingFence is exported and is the only LEADING-fence test; no /^---\r?\n/ survives as a test (one remains inside a doc comment on line 34). But grep -n -- "'---'" lib/personnel.js returns TWO code lines, not one: line 40 inside hasLeadingFence, and line 54 inside the parseFrontmatter loop, if (line.trim() === '---') — the CLOSING fence, a different test that F1 was never about. The property holds; the criterion as worded does not. I left the closing-fence line alone rather than reshape code to make a grep pass. Flagging it so the reviewer judges the wording, not me.
2. PASS — T1 passes; M1 reds exactly {T1, T3}; dirty-fixture case green under M1.
3. PASS — examined returned; T2 passes; missing dir yields { roster: [], skipped: [], sources: [], examined: 0 } asserted by deepEqual.
4. PASS — the Examined line is printed before the degradation branch and before the parsed line on every non-JSON path; the three amendments assert 5, 6 and 0 and pass.
5. PASS — M2 observed set matches the predicted set exactly (5 cases), bare root green.
6. PASS — T4 passes on the unmodified branch, with server.length === 2 asserted before any row compare.
7. PASS — M3 reds exactly {T4}; the AS-8 CLI roster case stays green.
8. PASS — T5 passes; observed TypeError against master org-chart.js before F4a was applied.
9. PASS — T6 passes; observed "who is departed" against master org-chart.js before F4b was applied.
10. PASS — org: orphan_reports_to names a departed manager as the reason is unchanged and green.
11. PASS — check-org --json is byte-identical to master on both fixture roots (repo: 1141 bytes, exit 1 both; org-clean: 661 bytes, exit 0 both), compared by running the branch binary and the master-checkout binary against the same roots.
12. PARTIAL — host half done: 474 pass, 0 fail. The counted compose --build receipt was NOT taken: docker is off PATH for the implementer in a headless tick. Pending on the orchestrator. Expected 470 (AS-100 receipt 464 + 6), and the host-minus-compose delta should be 4, same as master.
13. PASS — six files, all from plan section 3.

NOT DONE: the compose receipt only (above). Nothing else is outstanding; no scope was deferred.

Working notes and the full mutation log: scratchpad/developer-lena/AS-73/progress.md. Reviewer note under M6 — the plan asks Ruben to try a fifth fence malformation the plan did not name; worth knowing that the parser rejects a fence preceded by a blank line and rejects \r\n-only content the same way the classifier now does, but I did not add a case for either, so that probe is genuinely open.

Compose receipt (orchestrator, tick watcher:67350, 2026-09-11 ~08:04Z) for HEAD 3f96ab2: docker compose run --rm --build test from the AS-73 worktree by absolute docker path — 'Image asc-chat-test Building' / 'Image asc-chat-test Built', tests 474, pass 474, fail 0, exit 0. Same count as Lena's host run (474 = 468 + 6). Ruben reviews next tick; plan §10 names his M6 probe (a fifth fence malformation), and Lena's AC-1 grep-wording finding is his to judge.

VERDICT: PASS. No inline fixes; HEAD certified 3f96ab2 (feat/AS-73-org-gate-predicates, commits c775f16 + 3f96ab2). qa-ruben, tick watcher:93997, 2026-09-11 ~08:25Z. Read cold: plan, then diff, then my own runs; the implementer's comment and the auto-review artifact were read only AFTER my findings and battery were written to scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/ (AS-73-findings.md, AS-73-mutations.log).

FINDINGS FIRST (4 mine + 1 attributed; 0 blocking, 0 defects).
F-1 [convention: plan wording, non-blocking] AC-1's grep for the quoted fence in lib/personnel.js hits TWO code lines, not one: line 40 (inside hasLeadingFence) and line 54 (if (line.trim() === '---') return out; — the CLOSING-fence test inside parseFrontmatter's loop, which F1 was never about). The property AC-1 states is met: line 40 is the only LEADING-fence test, and the regex grep matches only the doc comment at line 38 — no /^---\r?\n/ survives in code. This is the finding Lena flagged for me to judge; my decision: the code is right, the criterion is mis-worded, and reshaping the closing-fence line to satisfy a grep would be the wrong fix. Recorded as pass-on-property. Proposed wording for the plan's owner (cto-owen): "hasLeadingFence is exported and is the only LEADING-fence test in the module: grep -n -- \"'---'\" lists exactly two code lines — the leading-fence test inside hasLeadingFence and the closing-fence test inside parseFrontmatter's loop — and grep -n '\\^---' matches only a doc comment."
F-2 [plan record, non-blocking] AC-12's compose expectation (470, "host-minus-compose delta 4") was derived from AS-100's receipt on b0763ad, not from the host baseline b1bba80; git log b0763ad..b1bba80 -- apps/chat/test shows AS-61 (6b14c38) and AS-72 (79d639d, 1ca6059, 5a362db, 57ebf2a) adding cases between the two commits. Observed: compose 474 = host 474, delta 0 — the healthy state (the test tree is the same on both sides). AC-12 says any other delta is a finding, so it is recorded — against the plan's arithmetic, not the branch. Post-merge expectation on master e5de119: 478 + 6 = 484 host.
F-3 [plan recipe, non-blocking] M1's "assert applied" as written (the file contains /^---\r?\n/ exactly once) is FALSE against the implementation: hasLeadingFence's doc comment quotes the old regex in prose, so the whole-file count after mutation is 2. My battery's site-anchored count (inside readPersonnel's body: 1; hasLeadingFence(text)) skipped: 0) is the assertion that proves the site. A verbatim follow of the recipe reports "mutation did not apply" on a mutation that did — the AS-95 sharpening, arriving one review later. Recipe should anchor to the enclosing function.
F-4 [note, out of scope] CR-only (classic-Mac) line endings: a VALID dossier written with \r alone is silently dropped by parser AND classifier (the whole file is one "line"; trim() of it is not the fence). Agreement holds — which is the property — and no live personnel file has this; pre-existing, not AS-73's. Recorded so nobody rediscovers it as a predicate disagreement.
F-5 [nit, attributed to the auto-review artifact, read after my findings; I did not raise it independently] test/roster-parity.test.js parses the CLI child's stdout with JSON.parse without first asserting exit status, so a CLI refusal surfaces as "Unexpected end of JSON input" with stderr lost. The guard still fails (never goes green), so diagnosability only. Not fixed inline: a nit taken from third-party output would have cost a compose retake. Suitable for AS-74 or any next touch of that file.
Disproved during M6, recorded so the next reviewer does not re-chase it: I suspected T4's work/moreTasks were trivial on the fixture root; they are not — test/fixtures/repo carries a .lattice with three tasks for agent:eng-ada (work is a real object, moreTasks 2).

M6 PROBE PAST THE LIST (agreement, not acceptance). 13 entries planted in a scratch root under tmpdir (real personnel/ never written): ---\r\n alone (the plan's example), fence preceded by a blank line, CR-only dossier, "--- \r\n" trailing-space CRLF dossier, double BOM, NBSP-prefixed fence, ----, empty file, whitespace-only file, "-\t--", clean dossier whose closing fence is CRLF, BOM then blank line then fence, and a DIRECTORY named dir.md. Result: examined 13 = 4 roster + 2 skipped (crlf-alone: malformed_frontmatter; dir.md: unreadable) + 7 no-fence; 0 disagreements in 13 between parseFrontmatter and hasLeadingFence; the invariant closes. The blank-line-first and CRLF-alone cases behave exactly as the plan's section 10 predicted. Script and output: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-73-m6-probe.{mjs,txt}.
Parity guard edges: direct mode is reached by resolution rule 4 (CHAT_DB set, no CHAT_API ⇒ no probe), so the live container on 8347 cannot leak into T4; rows are sorted by name on both sides via readRoster; self is the only stripped field, so a CLI that grew self would still fail the compare. What it does NOT compare: the CLI's table renderer (out of scope — the finding was row shape) and /api/org vs check-org --json (covered by AC-11's byte-identity, not by parity).
Merge seam (what else was in flight): master moved from b1bba80 to e5de119 during this branch's life (AS-81, AS-82 merged). Files master touched under apps/chat: test/stream.test.js, test/watcher-main.test.js, test/watcher-process.test.js, watch/advance-watcher.mjs, two export files — none of AS-73's six. git merge-tree --write-tree master feat/AS-73-org-gate-predicates produced a tree with no conflict entries. Clean seam.

MUTATION BATTERY (scratch copy of the worktree via fs.cpSync under my scratchpad; the worktree was never mutated; git status --porcelain in .worktrees/AS-73 empty at the end). Control in the copy: 474/474/0. Every mutation: sha256 before, anchored edit, applied-at-site asserted by split().length-1 counts, suite (TAP), exact failing set, restore, sha256 equal, suite green 474 again.
- M1 (lib/personnel.js, classifier back to the narrow regex; site proof: regex inside readPersonnel body 1, "hasLeadingFence(text)) skipped" 0): predicted {T1, T3}; observed {T1, T3} EXACT, 2 fail / 472 pass; "check-org: exits 1 and names every violation on the dirty fixture root" stayed green (control held).
- M2 (lib/personnel.js, increment deleted, examined = roster.length + skipped.length before the sole return; site proof: assignment inside readPersonnel 1, "examined++" 0): predicted {T1, T2, T3, exits-0-clean, exits-1-dirty}; observed that set EXACT, 5 fail / 469 pass; bare-root case green (control held).
- M3 (bin/chat.js, "reportsTo: e.reportsTo," deleted; site proof: 1 -> 0 in the file and 0 in the rosterRows(me){ … registerIdentity: slice): predicted {T4}; observed {T4} EXACT, 1 fail / 473 pass; "cli: roster prints the active company roster with work status (AS-8)" stayed GREEN — Priya's AS-33 survivor, now caught by one case.
3 mutants, 3 killed, 0 survivors, all three restores hash-proven. Log: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-73-mutations.log.

RECEIPTS. Host (worktree, node --test): tests 474, pass 474, fail 0, exit 0 — plan's 468 + 6. Compose, my own counted run with --build from .worktrees/AS-73/apps/chat by absolute docker path: "Image asc-chat-test Building" / "Image asc-chat-test Built", tests 474, pass 474, fail 0, exit 0 (scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-73-compose.txt); see F-2 for why 474 and not the plan's 470. Real root, read-only, branch binary with --root /Users/forrest/Code/american-software-company: "Examined 11 .md files in /Users/forrest/Code/american-software-company/personnel" / "10 active of 10 dossiers parsed, 0 unparsed" / "No violations." exit 0 — 11 directory entries, all .md (README + 10 dossiers), invariant 11 = 10 + 0 + 1. First time the gate states its own cardinality on live data.

ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA SWEEP — the floor check, after the findings above. Cardinality: 13 criteria examined; 6 files in the diff (exactly plan section 3); 474 host cases and 474 compose cases run; 3 mutants; 13 probe entries; 1 live root. Result: 13 of 13 met on property; 2 of those (AC-1, AC-12) carry plan-wording findings (F-1, F-2); 0 unmet; findings outside the list: 3 (F-3, F-4, F-5), none blocking.
1 property met, wording wrong (F-1). 2 PASS — T1 green; M1 red set exact; dirty-fixture green under M1. 3 PASS — examined returned; T2 green; missing-dir shape deepEqual'd four-key (T2 and my probe). 4 PASS — Examined line printed before the degradation branch and the parsed line; amendments assert 5/6/0 and pass. 5 PASS — M2 set exact, bare-root green. 6 PASS — T4 green on the unmodified branch; server.length === 2 asserted before any row compare (read in diff, line 92). 7 PASS — M3 reds exactly {T4}; AS-8 CLI case green. 8 PASS — I ran the branch's T5 against master's org-chart.js in a git-archive copy: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'status'). 9 PASS — same for T6: actual detail "reports to agent:mgr, who is departed". 10 PASS — the departed case is green on the branch and on the master copy. 11 PASS — check-org --json byte-identical master vs branch: fixtures/repo 1141 = 1141 bytes (exit 1 both), fixtures/org-clean 661 = 661 (exit 0 both). 12 PASS on numbers with F-2 on the expectation. 13 PASS — --stat: six files, no .lattice/, personnel/, fixtures, top-level markdown, package.json.

Not done by me: nothing outstanding on this branch. Routing: F-1/F-2/F-3 are plan-record notes for the plan's owner, no lifecycle action. Orchestrator: the AS-73 status transition and the --no-ff merge are yours; expected post-merge host count on e5de119 is 484.

Merged d815848 (--no-ff) into master from the main checkout after Ruben's PASS at 3f96ab2 (orchestrator, tick watcher:93997, loop tick 18). Post-merge: worktree .worktrees/AS-73 removed, branch deleted locally (never pushed; no PR was needed — no board ask on this diff). Ruben's plan-record findings stay on the record: AC-1 is met on property (one leading-fence test) and its grep wording over-counts the closing-fence test at line 54; AC-12's compose baseline was computed from AS-100's receipt rather than b1bba80 (observed host-minus-compose delta 0, healthy); M1's whole-file 'regex occurs once' assert is wrong because the doc comment quotes it — the site-anchored count is the proof. AS-74 (roster truncation guard) is now unblocked on the personnel/roster seam and is next by age. The chat deploy is the watcher's: dockerBin non-null and the container is serving desiredId, so it rebuilds unattended.
